extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators and parties preparing infringement contentions (plaintiffs/defense counsel) in district-court litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare a representative claim chart mapping each claim element of a patent (here U.S. Pat. No. 7,403,788) to accused products/systems and supporting factual documentary evidence for pleading/infringement contentions. The document explains each claim element and gives examples and factual support tying Culver Franchising System's websites, apps, POS systems, short codes, and privacy policies to those elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble — 'A system for enabling targeted content delivery to a mobile device...'
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim preamble: 'A system for enabling targeted content delivery to a mobile device, said mobile device having a device address, said device address having associated therewith at least one unique identifier, said system comprising:'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that Culver's provides websites, mobile apps, and point-of-sale systems (each a Point of Interaction or POI) that initiate communications enabling targeted content delivery to a mobile device (e.g., via SMS). Notes that each POI is separately accused as a separate channel of infringement. Identifies mobile device examples (phone, tablet) and device address examples (phone number). States that the unique ID can be a phone number or other device-identifying data. Includes screenshots of signup pages and SMS examples. Also notes that preamble infringement analysis should not be construed as admission that the preamble is limiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1a] 'a message application server'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines message application server as a server component that communicates with the POI and processes messages/requests to and from the POI. Cites Culver's privacy policy and documentation disclosing collection of names, addresses, phone numbers, mobile numbers and other information (used to process messages). Provides screenshots of privacy policy showing intended data collection and use to contact users and provide requested services.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1b] 'a trigger system in communication with said message application server, said trigger system comprising:'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1b] a trigger system in communication with said message application server, said trigger system comprising:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains Culver's trigger system as a component (combination of client-side web client and backend server, or server-end messaging application) configured to receive trigger signals and communicate with the message application server to generate and deliver targeted content. Provides examples including web client, backend server, server-end messaging application receiving short codes, and in-store POIs (POS terminals) that accept user input (mobile identifiers) and send notifications through backend servers. Includes screenshots of signup and POS receipt examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1c] 'a trigger client component configured to generate a trigger signal comprising a trigger action, user content request data and said at least one unique identifier'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1c] a trigger client component configured to generate a trigger signal comprising a trigger action, user content request data and said at least one unique identifier;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains trigger client component as the portion generating the trigger signal when a user inputs information (registers, makes a purchase, redeems a coupon, signs up for electronic receipts or rewards). Defines trigger signal components: trigger action (purchase request, coupon redemption/generation/verification, subscription, registration, offer generation/verification, service request, query), user content request data (purchase receipt, total price, discount, applicable offers, deliverable areas, product specs, quantity, etc.), and unique identifier (e.g., phone number). Notes that trigger client may run in background or be automatically received by webpage. Provides examples including short-code interaction and privacy policy text describing data obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1d] 'a trigger server component in communication with said trigger client component, said trigger server component configured to:'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1d] a trigger server component in communication with said trigger client component, said trigger server component configured to:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes Culver's trigger server as backend program code configured to receive and respond to messages and service requests from the POI/trigger client. States the trigger server component collects information (personal, browsing, device info) via POIs per the privacy policy. Provides examples of trigger server functionality and screenshots of privacy policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1e] 'receive said trigger signal'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that the trigger server component is configured to receive the trigger signal (which comprises trigger action, user content request data, and unique identifier). Describes that the trigger server manages and transfers the trigger signal and may store its components. Gives example where the trigger signal contains the mobile number as unique identifier and coupon code request data.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1f] 'send to said message application server said trigger signal for processing by said message application server'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1f] send to said message application server said trigger signal for processing by said message application server;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the trigger server component sends the trigger signal (unique identifier, user request data, trigger action data) to the message application server for further processing. Examples of processing include device address identification, storing trigger signal content, updating user information, and generating user-requested data.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1g] 'wherein said message application server is configured to:'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1g] wherein said message application server is configured to:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces the set of specific tasks performed by the message application server. The document explains that Culver's message application server performs the following listed tasks (detailed in subsequent elements): receive trigger signals, derive mobile device address, generate content based on user request data, and send generated content to the mobile device address. Emphasizes server-side processing and communication with POIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1h] 'receive from said trigger system said trigger signal, and in response thereto:'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1h] receive from said trigger system said trigger signal, and in response thereto:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that the message application server receives the trigger signal components and, in response, may store the trigger signal components and generate a response corresponding to the received trigger signal. The response may include mathematical, logical, or programmable operations on components of the trigger signal. Examples show storing unique identifier, user request data, and trigger action data and generating responses accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1i] 'derive said mobile device address from said at least one unique identifier'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1i] derive said mobile device address from said at least one unique identifier,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that the message application server derives the mobile device address (e.g., phone number) from the received unique identifier. Cites Culver's privacy policy and examples where the mobile number is both the unique identifier and the mobile device address.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1j] 'generate content based on said user request data'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1j] generate content based on said user request data, and
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that the message application server generates content/messages based on the user request data. Examples include messages mentioning offers/deals, customer support/relationship info, purchase receipts, requests for customer feedback, promotional codes, coupons, rewards offers, status of purchases, product information, invitations to surveys, app download offers, website links, store locator info, and other promotional/transactional messages. Screenshots of SMS offers and receipts illustrate generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1k] 'send said generated content to said device address of said mobile device'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1k] send said generated content to said device address of said mobile device;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the message application server sends the generated content to the mobile device address associated with the user's mobile device (e.g., via short codes/SMS). Reiterates types of content sent (offers, receipts, coupons, app links, product details, store locations, reminders, etc.) and provides SMS screenshots as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1l] 'an offer application component'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines an offer application component/system as software running in the background (web client, mobile app, point-of-sale terminal, or server) configured to facilitate validation, analysis, and redemption of offers received on the user's mobile device. Gives examples of where the offer application component may run (client-side, mobile app background, POS backend).

rubrics_metrics.name: [1m] 'an offer entry system in communication with said offer application component, and an offer database in communication with said offer application component for storing said generated content and said user request data, wherein said offer entry system is configured to:'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1m] an offer entry system in communication with said offer application component, and an offer database in communication with said offer application component for storing said generated content and said user request data, wherein said offer entry system is configured to:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the offer entry system as the system used to enter and redeem offers (front end and backend), communicating with the offer application component and an offer database that stores generated content and user request data. Provides many examples mapping offer types to systems: promotional code entry/redemption systems, coupon redemption systems, reward-points systems, discounted price systems, product purchase systems, download systems for apps, website/link access, store locator systems, etc. Notes in-store POS as an example of an offer entry system and includes screenshots/receipt evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1n] 'redeem said generated content'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the offer entry system is configured to redeem generated content. Explains that redemption depends on content type: promotional codes may be obtained, coupons redeemed, rewards provided, discounts applied, purchase status/info provided, product purchases completed, surveys/research performed, product reviews obtained, customer support provided, mobile apps made available, websites/links accessed, store locations provided, etc. Provides examples of in-store application of generated content at Culver's POS during purchase and scanned receipt images showing redemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: [1o] 'generate content redemption information comprising said redeemed content, and send said content redemption information to said offer application component for storage in said offer database'
rubrics_metrics.description: [1o] generate content redemption information comprising said redeemed content, and send said content redemption information to said offer application component for storage in said offer database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that the offer entry system generates redemption information when an offer is redeemed (information comprising the redeemed content) and sends that redemption information to the offer application component for storage in the offer database. Lists possible redeemed-offer types (promotional codes, coupons, rewards, discounts, purchase status, product info, rebates, account recovery offers, special deals, digital library access, legal info, app downloads, links, store locators, reminders, upgrades, etc.). Gives examples of redemption messages/text and screenshots/receipt evidence showing redemption records sent to storage.
